newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks finish at record high, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks finish at record high, seen firm.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares started the week at record heights, continuing to discount a strike by thousands of civil servants which dragged into its third week on Monday.
The key 57-share industrial index surged 40.96 points -- or 0.7 percent -- to close at a new all time high of 5,849.16.

"The market is looking very firm on fundamentals, that is prospects of lower inflation and interest rates," one broker said, referring to the central Reserve Bank's lowering last month of its key rediscount rate to 27.5 percent from 29.5 percent which fuelled hopes of lower interest rates.
"The market is still unaffected by the strike," another one added.

The strikers -- estimated by the Public Service Association at 70 to 80 percent of the country's 180,000 civil servants -- said on Monday they would not return to work until their jobs were guaranteed.

On the stock market on Monday, publishing group Zimpapers led the day's winners, surging 95 cents to 1,200, followed by cigarette manufacturer Rothmans and Alloys which rose 50 cents each to 2,500 and 800 respectively.

Sugar refinery ZSR gained 30 cents to 850, bankers Barclays rose 25 cents to 1,900, while clothing retailer Truworths at 635, cement producer Circle at 670 and winery Afdis at 270 all put on 10 cents.
Tyre manufacturer Dunlop and conglomerate TA bucked the trend, easing five cents to 150 and 140 respectively.

In minings, gold producers Ashanti soared 500 cents to 15,000 while Rio Tinto jumped 100 cents to 3,350 and Wankie Colliery edged three cents up to 320. The seven-counter mining index rose 39.60 points to close at 1,317.63.
